findings.issue: Shell-safe canonical quoting does not make configuration safe for Makefile include/export. Raw escaped dollar/parenthesis pass parser, decode to a literal Make shell function, and execute when Make consumes/export-evaluates it.
findings.evidence: Actual pure-temp /usr/bin/make include/export with an external recipe created a task-owned harmless marker. Explicit variable use and eager PORT-style assignment also created it. No repository target/database/provider was run.
findings.minimal_fix: Reject Make-active dollar characters in parsed values before canonical configuration is written, or use a separate proven data-only Make boundary. Add actual temp Make include/export/eager-use regressions; do not rely only on shell-source tests.

findings.issue: Recursive mode validates ledger database/template/state but never the permitted package. A child can request another Go package and reuse the original package clone.
findings.evidence: With ledger.package=example/permitted, fake ordinary go test example/different is accepted (exit0) and forwards against the same clone.
findings.minimal_fix: Resolve the recursive requested package under the selected working directory/build flags and require it matches the allocation's package permit. Refuse missing/mismatched package records before test execution; retain allowed same-package recursion and compile-only behavior.

nonblocking_notes.issue: Mode1 missing MULTICA_TASK_REAL_GO falls back to /opt/homebrew/bin/go. The fake probe confirms list/test commands use that default.
nonblocking_notes.interpretation: This is weaker explicit tool selection, not by itself a bypass of DB isolation: template validation and per-package clone/evidence still execute. The selected final launcher explicitly supplies REAL_GO. Tightening the ordinary-test configuration requirement is reasonable, but do not classify the observed path as default-business-DB access.

nonblocking_notes.issue: The first include/export probe used only a nonconsuming @: recipe and produced no marker. It did not cover the actual relevant value/environment consumption.
